description:
FOUND s494 (Fable, 2026-09-21) by the early-review probes for s492b (~/pcl-agent-scratch/s494/review/s492b/fh1.pl, fhs-*.pl); identical on main 9205d675 and on the agent's tree, so it is NOT the batch's.  perl 5.40.3 vs PCL:
    printf STDOUT ("A %s\n", "x");        perl: A x          pcl: dies  Undefined subroutine &main::STDOUT called
    print STDERR ("to stderr\n") if 1;    perl: prints       pcl: dies
    say STDOUT ("G say");                 perl: G say        pcl: dies
    my @l = ("a","b","\n"); print STDOUT (@l);   perl: ab    pcl: dies
  RIGHT today (the sibling spellings -- read how THEY reach the handle slot, rule 11): `printf(STDOUT "E %s\n", "x")`, `printf STDOUT "F %s\n", "x"`, `print $fh ("a","b")`, `print {$fh} (...)`.  (`printf $fh ("%s-%s\n", "a", "b")` printed "b" on main -- the scalar-comma leak -- and is FIXED by s492b's #2004.)
REACH, measured: ZERO sites in lib/, perl-tests/, cpan-tests/, the everyday corpus and the Rosetta corpus (which is why nothing ever saw it); 88 sites in 4 .pm files of perl's own lib/ + cpan/ tree.  A style some codebases use throughout (`printf STDERR ("...", ...)`), so a program written that way dies on its first diagnostic.
PERL'S RULE: after print / printf / say, a bareword followed by `(` is a FILEHANDLE unless a sub of that name is already known -- `sub foo {...} print foo ("x")` is `print(foo("x"))`.  PCL has that question answered in ONE place already: the three-valued callable classifier of #266 ("a bare NAME is a CALL only where it is CALLABLE").  FIX SHAPE: in the print-family's handle detection (`_is_print_term_start` and its caller -- the list-operator filehandle family in CLAUDE.md rule 11's own example), a bareword + `(` is a handle when the classifier does not say `yes`; STDIN / STDOUT / STDERR need no special list if the rule is "not callable".  Count the parse paths (statement level, inside parens `foo(print STDERR ("x"))`, with a statement modifier, in a block form) -- one fix upstream of all of them.
WHAT COULD BREAK -- probe each vs perl: `print foo ("x")` with `sub foo` declared BEFORE and AFTER the call (perl: before = call; after = handle, with a warning); `print uc ("x")` / any BUILTIN name (a call, always); `print Foo::bar ("x")` (qualified: a call if it exists); `print CONSTANT ("x")` with `use constant`; `print STDERR (1+2)*3` (perl prints 3 to STDERR and warns -- the classic; PCL should match the value); `print STDOUT;` (prints $_).
BAR: fh1.pl rows A-H = perl; a guard file's rows for the break list; corpus-diff IDENTICAL expected (zero sites) => no gen bump; gate.
SIZE: filler, about an hour.
subject: LOUD (pre-existing): a BAREWORD filehandle followed by a PARENTHESISED list is parsed as a function call -- `print STDERR ("x\n");`, `printf STDOUT ("%s\n", $v);`, `say STDOUT ("x");`, `print STDOUT (@l);` die "Undefined subroutine &main::STDERR called" (emission `(p-print (p-list-ctx (pl-STDERR ...)))`)
